title: The Saviors proves you don’t need to cast adults in child roles- you ...
transcript: This play took a massive risk by casting two actual 14 year olds as its leads. The play is called the saviors and follows two altar boys, Michael and Paul, as they grapple with their faith, their sexuality, their morality. Playwright Bubba Weiler has really proven himself to be a master at writing really complex, grounded characters. And so finding 14 year olds that can understand the complexity of this story and these characters, I'm sure was no easy feat. But these two actors, Ivan Howe and Julius Rinzel, are certainly up to the challenge. And having these roles played by actors who are so young adds a whole other layer to this piece. Like I said, Bubba Weiler writes really naturalistic dialogue and so his writing in combination with the very realistic looking church set and having young actors in these roles really does lead to this overall sense of realism. Adults playing children has become very commonplace and to be honest, it's become a bit of a theatre pet peeve for me. It just always takes me out of it. And so I love that this show kind of says no, actually, you can cast young actors that can handle these complex and heavy roles. As for the play itself, I was really excited about this one. As someone who loved Weiler's previous play, well, I'll let you go. That was literally my favorite play that I saw last year and was also directed by Jack Serio, who is Directing the saviors. And so to see that team come back together on a new play was very exciting to me. And while I don't think this one is quite as strong as well I'll let you go, I do think that there is a lot to like. I really liked what it had to say about youth and the role that religion can play in young lives, both positive and negative. In fact, I think it's incredibly nuanced in its discussion of religion and faith. But in doing so, I found its ultimate conclusion to be a bit unsatisfying. No spoilers, obviously, but it is very open ended and I just wanted a little bit more of a resolution. But it does give you a lot to chew on and it is a play that I will probably be thinking about for a little while. With this play, I think that Bubba Weiler has really proven that he is a playwright to watch. And his really excellent writing and characterization, along with the solid performances from our two young lead performers, performances from our two adult actors, which I didn't even mention, but they're excellent as well, and all brilliantly shepherded by Jack Serio. The Saviors is going to be a Broadway Ben recommendation.
